sentences.text: 2. Appellants are the petitioners and respondent is the respondent in the O.P. BRMR,J 3.
Notice got issued to respondent in the appeal is served but none appeared.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the learned Tribunal erred in taking the age of the appellant No.2 - petitioner No.2, erroneous applied the multiplier, erred in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.50/- per day instead of Rs.200/- per day, awarded less amounts under different heads and prayed to enhance the same.
5. Appellants - petitioners have filed claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum on the death of the Mohd. Nizamuddin And Another vs Apsrtc, Rep.

By Md, Musheerabad, Hyd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32304573/
1 deceased Mohammed Rahaman @ Shafi.
6.
Appellants have challenged the quantum in the appeal.

7. The learned Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.50/- per day, arrived monthly income at Rs.1,500/- (50 x 30), arrived annual income at Rs.18,000/- (1,500 x 12), deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses and arrived at Rs.12,000/- [18,000 - (1/3rd of 18,000 = 6,000)], applied multiplier '11' and arrived at Rs.1,32,000/- [12,000 x 11].

Further, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses and the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is Rs.1,39,000/- rounded BRMR,J off to Rs.1,40,000/- and awarded interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of realization.

8. Appellants - petitioners have stated in the claim petition that the deceased Mohammed Rahaman @ Shafi is aged about 19 years as on the date of accident, was working as motor mechanic and earning Rs.6,000/- per month.

9. PW3 - M.Sudhakar Reddy is the co-employee of the deceased, he deposed that the deceased used to work as electrical motor mechanic at Marikal village, used to earn Rs.200/- to Rs.300/- per day by repairing bore well motors, water motors, grinders and mixer motor and other motors.
Though PW3 was cross-examined nothing incriminating could be elicited from him.
10. The learned Tribunal ought to have granted reasonable amount towards the income of the deceased.
This Court is of the view that if an amount of Rs.4,000/- per month is taken towards income of the deceased, which will meet the ends of justice.

Appellants are entitled for future prospects, consortium as per the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 1.
(2017) 16 SCC 680 BRMR,J 11.

sentences.text:
In the result, MACMA.No.3760 of 2008 is allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced as under:
a) The impugned award dated 01.06.2007, passed in O.P.No.701 of 2005, stands modified.

(2009) 6 SCC 121 (2019) 17 SCC 465 BRMR,J b) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.1,40,000/- is enhanced to Rs.7,14,800/- together with costs and interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing the petition till payment.
c) Appellants - petitioners are directed to pay court fee on the enhanced amount.

d) Respondent is hereby directed to deposit the awarded amount with interest and costs less the amount already paid if any within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

e) Appellant Nos.1 and 2 - petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled for an amount of Rs.3,57,400/- each and they are permitted to withdraw their entire share amount with costs and interest thereon without furnishing security.

Interim orders if any shall stand vacated, miscellaneous application/s pending if any shall stand closed.
